title: Lamb Tagine
blurb: Slow-braised with apricots and warm spice, finished with cinnamon-toasted almonds.

ingredients.name: bone-in lamb stew meat or neck, cut into 1½-inch pieces
kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed

steps: Toss the lamb with 2 tsp (5.6 g) of the salt in a large bowl. Hold at room temperature for an hour, or refrigerate up to a day.
Bring the stock to a boil in a small pot, pull it off the heat, drop in the apricots, and leave them to soften for at least 15 minutes.

Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Warm the oil over medium heat in a tagine, Dutch oven, or heavy pot with a tight lid. Brown the lamb in batches with space around each piece, roughly 10 minutes per batch, moving finished pieces to a plate.

Pour off the rendered fat, leaving a thin film in the pot. Add the onions and ¼ tsp (0.7 g) salt and cook until soft, about 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, fresh ginger, one cinnamon stick, saffron, ground ginger, turmeric, pepper, ground cinnamon, and nutmeg, and cook until aromatic, about 2 minutes. Return the lamb with its juices, then add the apricots, stock, and half the cilantro. Seal with foil and the lid (foil is unnecessary in a tagine) and cook in the oven 2½ to 3 hours, turning the meat now and then, until tender. Correct the seasoning.

While it cooks, melt the butter with the second cinnamon stick in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the almonds and ¼ tsp (0.7 g) salt and toast to golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick.

Transfer the lamb and its juices to a platter. Scatter over the almonds along with the skillet butter, then the scallions, parsley, and remaining cilantro. Finish with lemon juice. Serve with flatbread or couscous.

title: Marinara Sauce
blurb: Sweet onion and whole tomatoes, simmered down an hour and blended smooth.

ingredients.name: Vidalia or other sweet onions, very coarsely chopped
kosher salt, plus more to taste
freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onion and garlic, stirring now and then and keeping them from browning, until aromatic, about 3 minutes. Stir in the oregano.
Crush the tomatoes by hand and add them to the pot with all their juices. Season with the salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then drop to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced, about 1 hour.
Off the heat, blend smooth with an immersion blender. Correct the seasoning.
note: Per 1-cup serving, estimated. Diamond Crystal assumed. Canned tomato sodium varies widely between brands; unsalted tomatoes drop it to roughly 380 mg. Keeps 5 days airtight in the refrigerator, or 6 months frozen. The garlic goes in whole and gets blended at the end; crush it first if you want it sharper.

title: Coq au Vin
blurb: Marinated overnight in Burgundy, braised with lardons, and finished with glazed pearl onions and fried croutons.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
hearty red wine, Burgundy for preference
lardons, pancetta or bacon, cut into ¼-inch dice
extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more as needed
white or brown mushrooms, sliced, halved first if large
white bread, crusts removed, cut into triangles
chopped parsley, plus more to finish

steps: Season the chicken with 2¼ tsp (6.3 g) of the salt and the ½ tsp pepper. Put it in a large bowl with the wine, bay leaf and thyme, cover, and refrigerate. Two hours will do; overnight is better.
Render the lardons in a Dutch oven over medium-low heat until crisp and golden, 10 to 15 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto paper towel and leave the fat in the pot.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade, keeping the liquid. Dry the pieces thoroughly, or they will steam rather than brown. Bring the rendered fat to just short of smoking over medium heat and brown the chicken in a single layer, working in batches, 3 to 5 minutes a side. Add oil if the pot runs dry. Move each piece to a plate as it colours.

Into the same pot go the diced onion, carrot, half the mushrooms, and the remaining ¼ tsp (0.7 g) salt. Cook about 8 minutes until lightly browned, scraping up the fond as you go and dropping the heat if anything threatens to catch.

Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for a minute, then the flour for another. Off the heat, push the vegetables to one side, pour the brandy into the clear space and light it. If that makes you nervous, simmer it off for a minute instead. Once the flame dies, pour in the reserved marinade, bring to a boil, and reduce by half to about 1½ cups (360 ml), roughly 12 minutes, skimming any large pockets of foam.
Return the chicken with its juices and half the lardons. Cover and simmer gently for an hour, turning the pieces once. Uncover and simmer 15 minutes more to thicken. Correct the seasoning.

While that cooks, melt 1 tbsp (14 g) of the butter with 2 tbsp (27 g) of the oil in a skillet over medium-high. Add the pearl onions with a pinch of sugar and a little salt, cover, drop to low, and cook 15 minutes, shaking the pan often. Uncover, push the onions aside, add the remaining mushrooms, and raise the heat. Cook 5 to 8 minutes until browned, stirring the mushrooms and tossing the onions now and then. Take both out and wipe the pan.

In the same pan, melt the remaining 2 tbsp (28 g) butter with 1 tbsp (13 g) oil over medium heat until foaming. Fry the bread until golden, about 2 minutes a side, adjusting the heat so it does not burn. Salt the croutons as they come out.

Add the pearl onions, mushrooms and remaining lardons to the pot and baste everything in the sauce. Dip each crouton in the sauce and then into the parsley. Scatter the rest of the parsley over the dish and set the croutons on top.
note: Per serving, estimated. Bone-to-meat ratio is assumed at 65 percent edible yield, and the fat figure assumes the rendered lardon fat stays in the pot. Sodium is driven by the cured pork and the salt brand; Diamond Crystal assumed. Alcohol is taken as cooked off, with residual wine sugars counted in the carbohydrate.

title: Oven Risotto with Crispy Mushrooms
blurb: Baked rather than stirred, topped with mushrooms roasted until they crisp.

ingredients.name: mixed wild, shiitake, or crimini mushrooms, sliced ¼ inch thick
extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling
chicken stock or low-sodium broth, divided
cold unsalted butter, cut into pieces

steps: Set racks in the bottom third and middle of the oven and heat to 350°F (175°C). On a rimmed baking sheet, toss the mushrooms with the garlic, thyme, red pepper flakes, ¼ cup (54 g) of the oil, and ½ tsp (1.4 g) of the salt. Roast on the bottom rack, tossing once halfway, until deeply golden and crisp, 25 to 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tbsp (27 g) oil in a large ovenproof Dutch oven over medium-high. Cook the onion, stirring often, until softened, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in the rice and season with the black pepper and ½ tsp (1.4 g) salt. Cook until some grains turn translucent, about 2 minutes. Add the vermouth, bring to a simmer, and cook until the pan is nearly dry, about 2 minutes. Add 2½ cups (600 ml) of the stock, bring to a simmer, then cover and bake on the middle rack until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the rice is still slightly firm at the center, 16 to 18 minutes.

Return the pot to the stove over medium heat. Add the remaining ½ cup (120 ml) stock and cook, stirring constantly, until the rice is tender with some bite and the sauce is creamy, about 2 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the Parmesan, butter, and lemon zest, and season with the remaining salt to taste. Loosen with a little warm water if needed; it should be thick but pourable.
Turn out onto a platter, top with the crispy mushrooms and parsley, drizzle with oil, and serve with lemon wedges.
note: Per serving, estimated. Diamond Crystal assumed. Fat is high because the full quarter cup of roasting oil is counted, though some stays on the sheet. The mushrooms finish before the rice; leave them on the sheet rather than covering them, or you undo the crisping.

title: Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb
blurb: Seared, crusted with garlic and soft herbs, roasted to medium-rare.

ingredients.name: frenched lamb, 8 ribs each, trimmed to a thin fat cap

steps: Heat a 12-inch heavy skillet over high heat until hot, at least 2 minutes.

Pat the racks dry and rub them all over with 1½ tsp (4.2 g) of the salt and ¾ tsp (1.5 g) of the pepper. Add the vegetable oil to the skillet and sear the racks, in two batches if needed, until browned on all sides but not the ends, about 10 minutes per batch. Move them to a small roasting pan.
Set a rack in the middle of the oven and heat to 350°F (175°C).

Stir together the garlic, parsley, thyme, rosemary, olive oil, and the remaining ½ tsp (1.4 g) salt and ½ tsp (1 g) pepper. Coat the meaty side of each rack with the herb mixture, pressing it on. Roast 15 to 25 minutes, until a thermometer inserted diagonally into the center reads 125°F (52°C). Tent loosely with foil after 15 minutes so the frenched bones do not burn.
Rest, covered, 10 minutes; the temperature will carry to 130°F (54°C) for medium-rare. Cut each rack into 4 double chops.
note: Per serving of two double chops, estimated. The dominant variable is how thin the fat cap is trimmed, which can swing the fat figure by 15 g per serving either way; bone weight is excluded. The rub goes on before the sear, so a good deal of that salt ends up in the pan. Salt the racks an hour ahead and pat them dry before searing if you want the seasoning to land more predictably.

title: Braised Chicken with Olives and Harissa
blurb: Thighs marinated in harissa and ras el hanout, braised over onions and tomato.

ingredients.name: tomatoes, cored and cut into thin wedges
kosher salt, plus more for seasoning
green olives such as Castelvetrano, pitted and roughly chopped, divided

steps: Drizzle the oil into a large skillet with a tight-fitting lid and scatter the onions over it in an even layer. Lay the tomato wedges on top. Set aside.

In a large bowl, toss the chicken thoroughly with the harissa, ras el hanout, and salt. Arrange the chicken and any remaining marinade in a single layer over the vegetables. Scatter half the olives, the garlic cloves, and the cilantro over the chicken, then pour in the water and cover.
Set over high heat and cook just until the liquid simmers. Lower the heat to hold a simmer and cook, covered, until the chicken pulls apart easily with a fork, about 1½ hours.
If much liquid remains, uncover, leave the chicken in the pan, and raise the heat to high. Cook until the sauce thickens, swirling the pan occasionally so it does not scorch, 10 to 15 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining olives. Serve with rice, mashed potatoes, or crusty bread.
note: Per serving, estimated, based on 3¼ lb of thighs with the skin left on. Sodium is dominated by the harissa and olives, both of which vary sharply by brand, so treat that figure as the softest here. Rendered chicken fat is counted in the sauce rather than discarded.
